- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

requested_parts: whether same Town can generate Bringer Fear twice within one Tsunami use
answers.answer: No. A given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once within a single Power use, so the Town cannot generate nightmare-destruction Fear again when Tsunami’s threshold later damages it in the other Coastal land.

evidence.text:
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally. Apply these results separately to each would-be-destroyed Invader; the Fear result does not itself grant movement:

  | Would-be-destroyed Invader | Fear | Movement from this special rule |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Explorer | 0 | Push it. |
  | Town | 2 | Push it. |
  | City | 5 | No Push. |

  For each Invader that this Power use would destroy, gain **0/2/5 Fear for an Explorer/Town/City**, respectively; Push only the Explorer or Town. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions.
